verdict.rationale: React's docs describe an explicit data-in, UI-out model: components receive data and return what should appear, and React updates the screen when new data is passed in response to interactions (react-docs-24, react-docs-3). Components own their state (react-gh-1), and React Developer Tools let you inspect and edit props and state (react-docs-14), which supports tracing state changes. However, nothing in the pack explicitly documents one-way or unidirectional data flow, or contrasts it with two-way binding. missing for 10: explicit documentation of unidirectional data flow and props-down/events-up patterns, an explicit statement that React avoids implicit two-way bindings, independent or hands-on corroboration that state changes are easier to trace.
